# When Does Gravity Matter? A Transport-Regime Criterion for Microbial and Particulate Delivery in ECLSS Water Loops Across Earth, Mars, and Lunar Gravity

**Target track:** Environmental Control and Life-Support System (ECLSS) Technology, International Conference on Environmental Systems (see `docs/ices_target.md` for cycle-specific facts and their verification status).

**Status:** Draft manuscript, Phase 5 of an autonomous research program (`docs/decision_log.md` records the full provenance). This document is a modeling paper; every figure is machine-regenerated by `run.md`'s single command from the code in `/src/eclss_gravity`, itself pinned by 50 regression tests to the derivation in `docs/derivation.md` as corrected by an independent adversarial review (`docs/redteam_report.md`, `docs/limitations.md`).

## 1. Introduction

Environmental Control and Life-Support System (ECLSS) water recovery hardware — the ISS Water Processor Assembly (WPA), Urine Processor Assembly (UPA), and emerging Membrane Aerated Biofilm Reactor (MABR) architectures proposed for exploration missions — must tolerate persistent microbial colonization. ISS operational data documents recurring biofilm in WPA/UPA hardware, including direct recovery of biofilm from UPA flex lines (Zea et al., *Biofilm* 5, 2023) and a consistent set of Gram-negative genera (*Burkholderia*, *Ralstonia*, *Cupriavidus*, *Methylobacterium*, *Pseudomonas*) recurring across water-system microbiome surveys (Yamaguchi et al., *Sci. Rep.* 12, 2022). NASA's own modeling literature explicitly flags dormancy periods of up to one year — expected during transit or surface-mission gaps in crewed operation — as a distinct challenge for biofilm control (Li, Callahan et al., ICES-2020-42).

All of this operational and modeling experience is calibrated to Earth-gravity (ground testing, ISS microgravity) conditions. Lunar (0.17g) and Mars (0.38g) surface habitats, and the transit vehicles between them, introduce partial gravity as a new, unquantified variable for exactly the transport processes — sedimentation, buoyant convection — that determine whether suspended microbial biomass reaches, and stays on, a wall to form a biofilm. Whether this matters is not obvious a priori: it depends on how gravity-driven transport competes with the forced-flow and diffusive transport already present in pumped ECLSS hardware, and that competition has not, to our knowledge, been quantified for this specific class of hardware and organism population before this work.

**Relationship to prior art.** The general question — which transport mechanism (diffusion, interception, or gravitational sedimentation) delivers a particle to a wall in an engineered flow system — is not new. It is the founding decomposition of colloid filtration theory (Yao, Habibian & O'Melia, 1971), refined into the standard modern correlation for single-collector efficiency by Tufenkji & Elimelech (2004), and it is the same decomposition Belfort, Davis & Zydney (1994) used to explain the particle-size-dependent back-transport minimum in crossflow microfiltration. A closed-form deposition efficiency for gravitational settling in a horizontal tube — the exact geometry of Criterion 2 below — was published by Pich (1972). What is new here is not the decomposition but the addition of gravitational acceleration as an explicit, swept variable, evaluated at real ECLSS operating points and the specific particle-size populations (single cells through 500 µm sloughed aggregates) documented in spacecraft water systems, across the Earth-Mars-Moon range. A prior ICES paper (SAE 2009-01-2359, 2009) tested partial-gravity particle transport in a lunar-regolith water-filtration concept on NASA's reduced-gravity aircraft — the closest work found at the target venue — but did not derive a dimensionless criterion; it is a test protocol, not an analysis, and this work's inclined-clinostat validation suggestion (§6) draws directly on it.

## 2. Methods

### 2.1 System and operating points

We model a wetted channel segment of an ECLSS water loop carrying planktonic cells, aggregates, and a growth-limiting substrate, with a wall-attached biofilm layer. Four regimes span the operating envelope: a nominal pumped WPA line (13 lb/hr, sourced flow rate; 6.35 mm assumed tube diameter, swept 3.18–12.7 mm), a post-dormancy restart flush (10× nominal), a low-flow UPA feed line, an MABR shell-side flow, and a stagnant dead-leg/dormancy limit. Five particle classes span the documented size range: a single *P. aeruginosa*-equivalent cell (1.09 µm), a small aggregate (7 µm, matching the reported >80%-by-number detachment population), a median floc (100 µm) and large floc (183 µm, spanning the reported volume-dominant activated-sludge floc band), and a sloughed biofilm piece (500 µm, the reported upper detachment bound). Full parameter sourcing, with every value marked `[verified-existence]`/`[snippet-level]`/ASSUMED per its provenance, is in `docs/derivation.md` §1 and §8.

### 2.2 Transport velocities and criteria

Gravitational settling follows Stokes' law with a Schiller–Naumann drag correction engaged above particle Reynolds number 0.34 (validity enforced and warned-on in code, `criteria.py`). Hydrodynamic wall delivery is the larger of a Lévêque convective-diffusion solution (dominant for particles below a crossover radius `a_c` ≈ 3–32 µm depending on regime) and a geometric interception flux (dominant above it, where particle radius cancels exactly from the ratio). Three dimensionless criteria follow, each a ratio of a gravity-driven and a competing transport rate: `Ga_dep` (does gravity or flow dominate wall-normal *delivery*?), `Λ_g` (is the segment long enough for gravity to act before flow-through, i.e. the classical Hazen surface-overflow number, evaluated at full channel depth), and `Σ_g` (does gravity or shear dominate near-wall *retention*?). A wall-orientation factor `f_θ` (perimeter-averaged `1/π` default for a horizontal tube) converts the vertical settling velocity into a wall-normal flux. In the stagnant limit, buoyant convection is evaluated via the Rayleigh number against the classical critical value `Ra_c=1708` (valid for a vertical destabilizing gradient; see §5). Full derivations: `docs/derivation.md` §2–3.

### 2.3 Uncertainty propagation

A 10,000-sample Monte Carlo (fixed seed, `eclss_gravity.uncertainty.RNG_SEED`) propagates the dominant sourced/assumed uncertainties — a bimodal particle-size distribution (80% single-cell-scale, 20% floc-scale, matching the reported by-number/by-volume split), buoyant density ranges, tube diameter, and temperature — onto the crossover gravity level and `P(Ga_dep>1)`, reported separately per particle-size branch (§2.4 explains why combining them is misleading).

## 3. Results

**Figure 1** (`results/figures/fig1_regime_map_size_vs_g.png`): `Ga_dep` and `Λ_g` as functions of particle diameter and gravity level for the nominal WPA line. The `Ga_dep=1` contour crosses the Earth-Moon gravity band near 1 µm particle diameter; above ~13 µm (the crossover radius `a_c`), `Ga_dep` is essentially size-independent and gravity-dominant down to milli-`g`.

**Figure 2** (`fig2_g_star_vs_diameter.png`): sensitivity of the single-cell crossover gravity `g*` to the one significant ASSUMED geometric parameter (tube diameter). `g*` ranges from 0.12 to 0.48 `g_E` across the plausible 3.18–12.7 mm tube-diameter range — the qualitative finding (comparable order of magnitude across Earth-Moon) is robust to this assumption; a precise crossover value is not.

**Figure 3** (`fig3_dormancy_biofilm_accumulation.png`): a 1-year dormancy simulation in a 6.35 mm line. Deposition *rate* (time to reach a given deposited mass) differs by ~1700× between Earth/Mars (buoyant convection active, `Ra>Ra_c`) and Moon (convection suppressed, `Ra<Ra_c`, unopposed settling) — a genuine, transport-driven, gravity effect. The long-time (1-year) accumulated mass, however, converges to within a few percent across all three gravity levels, because biofilm growth kinetics (deliberately modeled as gravity-independent — see §5) dominate the overall timescale once any deposit has seeded, which happens within days at every gravity level tested. **This result was corrected after an implementation bug (an omitted growth term) produced a spurious ~10⁵× ratio in an earlier version; see `docs/limitations.md` §2.**

**Figure 4** (`fig4_convection_switch_narrow_line.png`): the Rayleigh-number mechanism behind Figure 3's rate effect. At a representative 1 K cabin-to-line thermal gradient, a 6.35 mm line convects at Earth and Mars gravity but not at lunar gravity (`Ra`=4953/1873/818 vs. `Ra_c`=1708); a 0.30 m tank convects unconditionally at all three gravity levels tested. This switch requires a vertical destabilizing gradient (§5) and sits within roughly one decade of the assumed `ΔT`, both important caveats on how load-bearing this specific mechanism should be treated as.

**Figure 5** (`fig5_monte_carlo_g_star.png`): Monte Carlo results, reported per particle-size branch. For single non-motile cells, `P(Ga_dep>1)` = 0.61 (Earth), 0.30 (Mars), 0.12 (Moon) — genuinely ambiguous, order-of-magnitude-comparable delivery across the whole range, not a sharp threshold. For flocs/aggregates, `P(Ga_dep>1)` = 1.00 at every gravity level tested — gravity dominates aggregate delivery unconditionally over the sampled parameter space.

**Figure 6** (`fig6_duty_cycling.png`): the operationally realistic case that a single fixed regime cannot represent — an alternating pumped/stagnant duty cycle rather than a continuously-pumped or continuously-dormant line. Deposited mass follows the same growth-kinetics-dominated trajectory as the pure dormancy case, with Earth and Mars tracking almost identically and lunar gravity slightly lower, corroborating Figure 3's conclusion from an independent scenario. The duty-cycle fraction itself is an assumed illustrative schedule, not a sourced ISS operating spec, and is labeled as such.

**Rising (negatively-buoyant) aggregates** (`results/data/rising_aggregate_comparison.csv`): the sourced biofilm wet-density range extends below water density (898 kg m⁻³, i.e. `Δρ ≈ −99` kg m⁻³ against water's 997), so gas-entrapping biofilm fragments rise rather than settle. The criteria are sign-symmetric — `|Ga_dep|` is unchanged for equal `|Δρ|` — but the deposition *location* inverts: such fragments accumulate on the **top** wall of a horizontal line. Every figure in this work plots only the sinking case, so any sampling or sensor strategy that assumes bottom-wall accumulation would systematically miss this population.

**Structural sensitivity checks** (`results/data/sensitivity_checks.csv`): two results materially qualify the conclusions above and are stated here rather than buried. (i) The biofilm *detachment* timescale is ~300× sensitive to an unresolved disagreement in the source literature over whether loss rate scales linearly or exponentially with shear — 20 days at `n=1` versus ~16 years at `n=3` — so no claim about deposit persistence is defensible to better than two orders of magnitude. (ii) Figure 4's three-way gravity separation does not survive a factor-2 error in `Ra_c`: at `Ra_c × 2`, still inside the geometric uncertainty assumption A18 already concedes, Mars also falls below onset and the result degrades to a two-way Earth-versus-rest split. This is why §6's validation plan prioritizes measuring `Ra_c` for tube geometry.

Headline numeric table: `results/data/regime_sweep_headline.csv`, reproduced by `scripts/run_regime_sweep.py`.

## 4. Discussion

**The size-selective floc transition is the sharpest, most design-relevant prediction.** `Λ_g` for the 183 µm floc class is 1.56 (Earth), 0.59 (Mars), 0.26 (Moon) at the nominal WPA line length — it settles out within the segment at Earth gravity and is carried through at Mars and lunar gravity. This means a lunar-surface or Mars-transit water line will transport aggregates to downstream components (filters, sensors, valves) that an Earth-gravity qualification test would show settling out upstream — a testable, falsifiable, and operationally consequential prediction that a 1g ground campaign cannot by itself reveal.

**For single non-motile cells, the honest finding is ambiguity, not a specific crossover.** Gravitational and diffusive wall-delivery fluxes are within an order of magnitude of each other across the entire Earth-to-Moon range (Figure 5). This means neither "gravity is negligible for cells" nor "gravity dominates cell delivery" is defensible as a blanket design assumption at any of the three gravity levels considered — the gravity term must be carried in any predictive model, and a 1g qualification test is not a valid surrogate for this population either, just not for the reason originally hypothesized (a specific crossover point) but because the two mechanisms are persistently comparable.

**Motility is a first-order caveat, not a footnote.** The organisms motivating this work (*P. aeruginosa*, *Burkholderia*, *Stenotrophomonas*) are flagellated. Measured swimming speed for *Pseudomonas* exceeds gravitational settling by a factor of ~500 at Earth gravity and ~3000 at lunar gravity (`Ga_mot = v_s/v_swim` ≪ 1 in all cases). The single-cell `Ga_dep` results above apply to non-motile or motility-repressed cells and to all aggregates (too large to be flagellum-propelled); for actively motile planktonic cells, self-propulsion — not gravity — governs delivery at every gravity level tested. This mirrors an experimental result: wild-type cells deposit gravity-independently while non-motile mutants show a 10–40× top/bottom deposition bias (Korber, Lawrence, Zhang & Caldwell, *Biofouling* 2, 1990).

## 5. Limitations

Full account: `docs/limitations.md`. Summarized:

1. **No scholarly full text has been read in producing this program.** Every citation was found by search; content claims are search-snippet fidelity throughout. This is a standing, disclosed limitation of the environment this work was produced in, not a claim that the citations are fabricated (existence was independently corroborated for every load-bearing source), and it should be cleared before actual submission.
2. **The buoyant-convection mechanism (Figures 3–4) requires a vertical destabilizing thermal gradient, and its three-way gravity separation is not robust to the geometric uncertainty already conceded on `Ra_c`.** A real spacecraft line's thermal environment (cabin air, structure, adjacent heaters) will not generically produce a purely vertical gradient; a horizontal component removes the `Ra_c` threshold entirely. Separately, a one-at-a-time sensitivity check (`docs/limitations.md` §4) found that doubling `Ra_c` — still within the stated tube-vs-infinite-plane-layer uncertainty — degrades Figure 4's Earth/Mars-convecting-vs-Moon-not split to a two-way Earth-vs-rest split, since Mars sits only 10% above the nominal threshold. This mechanism should be read as a demonstrated, testable hypothesis under a stated geometric condition, not a robust general result.
3. **Deliberate scope decisions, not gaps:** kinetic parameters (growth rate, half-saturation constant, yield) are gravity-independent by explicit modeling choice, defended by an ESA flight experiment (BioRock) that found no gravity effect on final bulk cell concentration at simulated Mars gravity — a result this work's transport/growth decoupling is *consistent with*, not contradicted by, since BioRock measured bulk concentration, not spatial deposit distribution. The general spatial transport PDE was not implemented; the closed-form criteria (which do not require it to locate the regime boundary) and a 0-D stagnant-reactor reduction were.
4. **Detachment persistence is not defensible to better than two orders of magnitude** (see Results): the source literature disagrees on the shear-scaling exponent, and that disagreement propagates to a 20-day-versus-16-year spread in deposit lifetime. Claims in this work concern deposit *formation*, not persistence, for that reason.
5. **Individual-fundability constraint honored throughout:** every result above is reproducible on a laptop at zero marginal cost (`run.md`); no centrifuge, parabolic flight, or institutional facility is required for the core contribution.

## 6. Validation

See `/validation/README.md` for the complete assessment. The core contribution is validated computationally (internal consistency checks, independent adversarial re-derivation to ≤0.3%, comparison against published secondary data) and does not require new physical experiments to stand as a modeling contribution.

Where a cheap physical test would nonetheless add the most is specific and identified: **measuring the critical Rayleigh number for tube geometry.** The model assumes the classical rigid–rigid plane-layer value `Ra_c = 1708`; a tube is not a plane layer; and the sensitivity check above shows a factor of 2 here overturns Figure 4's conclusion. Because `Ra_c` is a dimensionless, gravity-independent threshold, this is measurable at Earth gravity — no centrifuge or parabolic flight — for approximately $150, using a 2–3 mm water layer (where the onset falls at a readily-measured 3–11 K rather than the microkelvin scale a deep vessel would require). The protocol pairs a shallow plane-layer control, which must reproduce 1708 or the apparatus is at fault, with a small-bore tube measurement that returns the correction factor directly. A second, optional stage uses an inclined clinostat as a fractional-gravity analog — following SAE 2009-01-2359 at this same venue — to check the size-selective floc transition qualitatively. The ingest and comparison script (`eclss_gravity.validation_compare`) is written and tested against synthetic data with known onsets, so an experimenter needs to write no code.

## 7. Conclusions

Applying an explicitly gravity-parameterized version of a 50-year-old colloid-filtration transport decomposition to ECLSS water-recovery hardware operating points shows that (1) single non-motile planktonic cells experience genuinely ambiguous, order-of-magnitude-comparable gravitational and diffusive wall delivery across the full Earth-to-Moon gravity range, meaning 1g ground qualification is not a valid surrogate for this population at any gravity level tested; (2) aggregates and flocs above ~7 µm are gravity-dominated by 2–3 orders of magnitude regardless of gravity level, with a sharp, size-selective, falsifiable carry-through transition in the 100–200 µm band across the lunar-to-Mars window; and (3) in stagnant dormancy scenarios, gravity governs the *rate* of biofilm establishment (up to ~1700× difference) far more robustly than it governs the eventual steady-state outcome, which is set by gravity-independent growth kinetics. These are modeling results, reproducible from a documented single command, that identify specific, testable design and qualification-testing implications for lunar and Mars ECLSS water hardware.
